QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_44

question.text: Ujala Solar Pvt Ltd (a Section 8 FPE) has attracted interest from 'Bharat Impact Fund I', an EXISTING Social Impact Fund not launched exclusively for SSE-listed NPOs. If Bharat Impact Fund I has investable funds of Rs 500 crore, what is the MAXIMUM amount it may invest in securities of NPOs registered or listed on an SSE?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.3 'Social Impact Funds' bullet (a), 'Existing Social Impact Fund may invest 25% of their investable funds in securities of NPOs registered or listed on a social stock exchange.' 25% of Rs 500 crore = Rs 125 crore. The 100% threshold (option C) applies ONLY to SIFs launched exclusively for registered/listed NPOs. Note: Ujala Solar is a Section 8 FPE, but the 25% rule covers 'NPO securities on SSE' — and Section 8 companies are classified as NPOs, so the rule applies. (If Ujala Solar were a non-Section-8 FPE it would be in 'social enterprise securities' at 75%.) The Trap: Option B (75%) confuses with the FPE-side rule in Section 2.3.2.1 (75% in SV/SE unlisted securities). Option C (100%) applies only to exclusive SIFs. Option D invents 5%. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D/E treats Cat I AIF investment conditions — the 25%/75%/100% distinctions are frequently tested. XV (RA) uses similar caps in valuing SIF holdings. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When auditing a mixed-portfolio SIF, tabulate each holding by SSE-registration status; if the SIF is non-exclusive and its SSE-NPO exposure exceeds 25%, flag a potential AIF-regulation breach in the SIR — this has material implications for the SIF's impact attribution to your NPO client's program.
